title: International mobility is widespread but still selective, while climate disruption and pathway design redistribute migration risk
source_unit: IOM World Migration Report 2026, chapters on global migration, regular pathways, climate mobility, and internal displacement
geography: Global international migration, climate mobility, regular migration pathways, and internal displacement

observations.period: Mid-2024 stock and end-2024 displacement; World Migration Report 2026 global overview

denominator.unit: approximate world population reference for contextualizing the international-migrant stock

internal_displacement_end_2024.unit: people living in internal displacement globally by the end of 2024, approximately

international_migration_share_context.unit: approximate percent of world population represented by 304 million international migrants

mobility_pattern.value: Cross-border movement remains the exception rather than the norm; most people live in their country of birth and internal migration is more common

observations.method: IOM synthesizes UN and other official migration and displacement statistics, migrant-group data, regional evidence, and thematic analysis in its flagship World Migration Report.
observations.uncertainty: Migrant stocks and internal-displacement counts use different definitions, reference dates, and reporting systems. Aggregate stocks do not measure legal status, route risk, duration, household welfare, or whether movement was voluntary.
observations.subgroup: International migrants, migrant workers, students, refugees, asylum-seekers, internally displaced people, origin and destination communities, and governments managing mobility.
observations.counterinterpretation: Migration can expand income, skills, family security, cultural exchange, and development, while most international movement occurs through regular and relatively safe conditions. The global stock is not itself evidence of a crisis or a uniform trend in mobility.

observations.period: 2026 thematic analysis of regular pathways and climate mobility

denominator.unit: global migration-governance and climate-mobility policy framework

pathway_distribution.value: Regular migration pathways are increasingly selective and unequally distributed across regions, countries, and groups, reflecting development inequalities, visa regimes, and geopolitical relations

restrictive_policy_route.value: Restrictive policies can displace rather than reduce mobility, pushing people toward riskier, more precarious, and irregular journeys

climate_mobility_route.value: Climate change reshapes mobility through sudden disasters and slow-onset degradation; responses remain too reactive and disconnected from long-term adaptation planning

local_governance_route.value: Local governments, communities, Indigenous peoples, diasporas, civil society, and private actors are identified as central to climate-mobility responses

observations.method: IOM combines global evidence, regional case studies, migration-governance analysis, climate-mobility scholarship, and local/community perspectives across thematic chapters.
observations.uncertainty: Global projections and thematic summaries do not identify a universal climate-migration effect or prove that pathway restrictions caused a particular route. Local conditions, adaptation, wealth, conflict, legal status, and data gaps shape outcomes.
observations.subgroup: People considering or undertaking migration, marginalized and climate-exposed communities, migrants using regular or irregular pathways, local governments, Indigenous peoples, diasporas, employers, and civil society.
observations.counterinterpretation: Regular pathways can widen rights, health access, labour-market opportunity, remitting, and investment, while local adaptation can reduce forced movement. Restriction may sometimes address genuine protection or administrative constraints even if it also shifts risk elsewhere.

boundary: This record adds international-migrant stocks, pathway governance, climate mobility, local action, and internal-displacement framing. It is not respondent-level migration data, does not infer individual motives or route choices, and does not establish causal effects of climate or migration policy on displacement, welfare, or political behavior.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: IOM World Migration Report 2026 official chapter summaries retrieved through the IOM Publications Platform and search-indexed official pages; migrant-stock, internal-displacement, regular-pathway, restrictive-policy, climate-mobility, and local-governance claims cross-checked. Direct local page capture was restricted, so the digest records the retrieved evidence summary rather than a claimed local PDF hash.
